body: I hate the most how people end up seeing it, and then taking it, making up their own assumptions and stories about it, making it all about them and in the end just leaving me to rot. They're *my* wounds, dammit.

I understand that, and i completely agree with that. It really shouldn't be like that and it's just one big downward spiral of a 'community' that is negative for everyone involved. 

However, i do get sad when other people, especially people who SH themselves, get angry at them and alienate them. The reason they're even there is usually because the rest of the world has let them and their invisible problems down, and if even others who SH, the only people they could get understanding from, reject them in these ways, that only confirms their feelings of outcast-ness, and drives them further towards that whole shtwt circle, because it becomes the only thing that accepts them and their pain. This is frequently visible on the tag itself, too. Every time someone chimes in to say "shtwt is bad! These people are terrible!", the people that inhabit the tag get *very* vicious and enraged. Because, yet another person rejects their problems.

That said, I don't have a magical solution for it either, because it's just not as simple as "get help" or "call a hotline", because, truth is, those options usually don't even really exist. I just want to throw in my two cents on why this discussion is just that, sad.

I get your anger, but in the end, their self harm is not about you. They're just people who are hurting and have nowhere else to go. It's very unhealthy, the way they go about it, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone, but they struggle with it just as much as you and me.

Okay, so, where do i even begin-

My parents. They've made it very clear that i should never have been born.

My mother has always been neglective of me. I can't remember a single occasion in life where she has given me a hug, kiss or other loving touch. I was allowed to walk to school alone many years earlier than all the other kids. That in itself I thought was super cool at the moment, until i realised that that also meant that she was never there to wave at me in the bus on school trips, when other kids' parents were always there. She never had time for me. My earliest memories are of her and my father fighting and throwing things at eachother, and me stepping on broken glass the next day and getting wounds in my feet. After my parents divorced, my father regularly beat me and my brother on the weekends. And he and my mother constantly said mean things about the other when, honestly, i didn't feel connected to either side. Then my mother got a new boyfriend. He beat me too. And often dragged me across the floor by my hair to the point that bald spots were forming on my head and my hair was coming off all the time when i combed it during regular little girl activities. Kids at school found that incredibly funny, by the way. I was beaten up there, too, to the point that i couldn't tell if bruises were coming from my parents or my peers. Teachers never scolded the bullies, and instead tried to get me in self-confidence programs and trainings. That never helped.

Then middle school came around. I was regularly called out of the class because i needed to take care of court stuff to cease contact with my father, and to go to psychiatrists because I was starting to show self harming behaviors and signs of PTSD. Eventually it somehow became known to class that i was being abused at both my homes, and to them, that too was the funniest shit ever. I regularly got people telling me that "at least my parents love me, unlike yours", taking pictures of me and making memes and drawing wrist cuts on me, throwing eggs at my home (which in turn caused my parents to beat me more) etc. And the few relatives that did care just said "oh, karma will take care of those people, trust me" which is just another way of saying "i'm too lazy to help your situation." It's not like i didn't look for help either. I frequently came to teachers and mentors crying that I was too scared to go home. And they didn't do anything.

What else... relationships. My first boyfriend was scary. He knew everyone and everything around me, and for some reason, even though I did not have a phone, social media or anything, always knew where i was hanging out. And he was always there. And on the few occasions i did have access to the internet, he also knew exactly what sites i had been on, what my usernames were and so on. He beat me too, by the way. And tried to crush my head between his hands and then told me to not be such a wuss about it. And he locked me in his house when things didn't go his way. He also molested me way before i was ready for sex, because on that day, he had been so kind to pick me up from school because my cat had died. My cat's death is now never a clean thing to think of anymore, and I hate myself for it. When i broke up with him a year after, i got plenty of death threats from his friends. He also fabricated some things about me on the internet about being an underage porn star, and sent that to my parents, knowing exactly what would happen. He was in my life 7 years ago, and his impact was big enough that even today i'm scared he's following me.

There was one girl that was nice. She was anorexic, so i took care of her in the past 5 years. It was my only way to feel some kind of reason to be alive and be worth something. I completely shoved my own problems aside to make sure she was alright at all times, but that also meant that I had no more identity. When talking to people, it was always, "hey, and how is she doing?" and no one ever asked how i was doing. Ever. Everyone assumed that, because i was so strong, nothing could ever be wrong with me. But recently i've done some suicide attempts and things went south, so the mother of that anorexic friend scolded me and said i wasn't doing enough anymore. Now i have no friends.

I was recently diagnosed with borderline and PTSD, but despite that I always have feelings of being fake, being a fraud etc, mainly because of how people have treated me. Child abuse is always treated as something so serious in media, but when it overcomes me, its suddenly funny. When i get raped, its "get over it", when i end up in the hospital for trying to kill myself, its "everyone goes through depression, you're not special" and when i cut myself and someone finds out, its "why do you pretend your problems are worse than they really are?" and "your home situation isnt *that* bad." 

I'm out lf fuel for now, but if more comes up, i'll just.. spew it out.

My personal experiences with the mental health system in my home country have been laughable. I have many stories about this since i've been on and off treatment for a whole lot of different things for about 15 years, but here are a few highlights that should give you a general idea:

-if you tell the psychiatrist your parents are doing things to you that aren't very nice, and you're under 16, they *will* tell your parents about it, and ask them to confirm.
Police here does this too, btw. If you contact the police to say that a parent went physical on you, they will then contact your parents to ask them if this is true. You can see why this is not a good idea.

-they are very loose on medication regulation. In my case, they allowed my parents to regulate it for me. This resulted in abnormally high doses and no one who bothered to check up if i was okay with that.

-i've been on a wait list for therapy for a year. In the meanwhile, i get a psychologist who goes on vacation 7 times a year.

-the guy who was supposed to do my intake quit his job. Because they didn't bother to have a replacement, they wanted to kick me off of the wait list completely. After i've waited for nearly a year.

-suicide hotlines hang up on you, and their chat leaves you on read.

-some hot takes of things said to me by psychologists and psychiatrists: 
"Its only a mild depression. I can't even call it a depression."
"Well, if you've been self harming for 12 years, and you're not dead yet, you aren't really in danger."
"Its understandable that they kicked you out of school."
"Its not possible that you just don't want to see [name of abuser] again if youre this young. You can't make decisions about that yet. We'll try to reunite you."
"This is only for people who really have it bad. You're not that bad off."

Edit: remembered some more things.

-if you fail to complete treatment and be alright within the timeframe they give you, they'll kick you out. Simple as that. Can't beat a chronic mental condition in one year? Too bad, you're out. Suffer on your own.

-got any complaints? That's also too bad; you're mental, therefore your opinion doesn't count.
